title: Motivation Is the Gas Pedal. Logic Is Just the Steering Wheel
summary: Dr. Chris Gray is a clinical psychologist who left therapy for the research side of marketing and spent 30 years, including 15 at Saatchi & Saatchi, working out why people actually buy. In this episode he makes the case that every purchase, B2B included, traces back to an emotional need, and that logic is the steering wheel rather than the engine. He breaks down how to find that need with the five whys, why emotion-based messaging often looks completely rational on the surface, and what his Five Fs framework says about the relationships that survive a screw-up. Worth a listen for anyone running discovery with a buying committee, writing positioning, or working out what differentiation looks like once every product in the category does the job.
keyQuote: That emotional need is the spark. It is the gas pedal for why we buy. Rational thinking is the steering wheel that guides where we go.
guestBio: Dr. Chris Gray is a clinical psychologist turned consumer behavior researcher, keynote speaker, and consulting strategist. He finished his doctorate in clinical psychology in the late 1990s, ran his first focus group, and never went back to therapy. He spent roughly 15 years at Saatchi & Saatchi on brands including Coca-Cola, Adidas, Walmart, and The North Face before founding The Buycologist, a consumer psychology consultancy whose tagline is influence customer behavior without feeling gross. He writes the Substack Influence Without Feeling Gross, and his book, The Buycologist's Playbook, is due in 2027.
takeaways: Motivation is the gas pedal. Logic is only the steering wheel.
Emotion-based decisions usually look completely rational.
Ask a buyer why five times. The company reason comes first.
Your champion wants to look competent, and that is never in the RFP.
Manipulation wins one sale, then triggers psychological reactance.
Functional parity is coming for your category. Coffee got there first.
Information access stopped being an edge. Discernment replaced it.
